Introduction
This plugin uses region IDs to determine a player 'floor level'. Even autotiles can be drawn ABOVE players (if player is on lower ground). I have tried to find this type of plugin for a long time, then decided to code one my self.
I know you can use different tilesets or events to accomplish this, but this saves a lot of tiles in my tilesets. And no more event switches to toggle higher / lower ground.
Use event comments <lower> or <higher> to assign event floor level. If autotiles A3 (roofs) or A4 (walltop) tiles are used "Auto-assign" (no comments found) will assign the event to
higher
floor level
, else event is assigned to
lower
floor level
.
Also works (for example) with "
OcRam_Local_Coop
" and Yanfly engine -plugins (no issues known).
ps. You can use this plugin indoors as door passages also (shown later).
Here's what you need:
"OcRam_Passages" -plugin
Mark regions
RegionID 16 = Underpassage (this will set player to lower ground)
RegionID 17 = Overpassage (this will set player to higher ground, also draws B-E layers)
RegionID 18 = Cover tile for tiles B-E (transparent background)
RegionID 19 = Autotile Cover for A tiles (opaque background)
RegionID 20 = Always block passage (for blocking ie. door way sides)
RegionID 21 = Block passage AND draw tiles ABOVE, if on lower floor
RegionID 22 = Block passage to underpassage region (can be used to fix RMMV core "bug" where passable tile, like "bush", allows passage over cliffs)

Actually you don't even have to keep mouse button pressed. Clicking on region Id 18 is enough if player passes cover tile while player is on lower ground.
I'll try to explain:
Movement is blocked on region Id 18 while player is on cover tiles (and lower ground). Then path finding will start to find another way. When player leaves autotile region it finds shorter way (which was previously blocked) and the loop of paths is ready. Gladly player can interupt this anytime.
Possible solution:
If region Id 18 is needed only to block movement while on cover tiles I would use region Id 20 instead of 18. Region Id 18 should be used only to "elevate" player floor level (though by-product is blocking movement while on covers).
NOTE:
Region Id 20 will block movement also on higher ground level.
Please let me know if this was helpful.

I downloaded your plugin and found two issues with it (one I have fixed personally).
1) Like someone mentioned previously, while testing in my game, tiles were not correctly aligning if they were marked by a region set by the plugins Region ID values. This is most likely because the plugin is set up to work with MV's default 48x48 sprite/tile system. I went in to the plugin itself and proceeded to find all values labelled "24" and "48" and replaced them with "16" and "32" to correctly align them in a 32x32 format (my project is converted from VXAce and this is required).
2) It's too restrictive to what Region ID's you have set in the plugin. What I mean by this is that unlike Khas's Ultra Lighting or Yanfly's Region Restrictions plugins, it does not provide the ability to setup which regions to use in the maps "Note" box.
To give you an example of what I'm talking about. Say that you're using Khas Ultra Lighting plugin and you have one map that has a bridge that's 2 tiles high off the ground and on another map, there's a bridge that's 3 tiles high off the ground. Khas plugin is designed to align the "shadows" height depending on which region you've marked by a value of 10 (eg = Region 15 -> 1 tile high | Region 32 -> 3 tiles high). Without this functionality, you're restricted to the regions via the plugins settings rather than being able to adjust on-the-fly depending on the map.
Could you look in to adding the functionality within the maps Note box instead of being forced to use the plugins settings instead?

If a map is 256x256 (or larger if using modified values), the game will outright crash when attempting to load the map (this also happens in a new test project with just Khas's plugins and yours). This is most likely caused by the exact same problem that happened a while back with Ultra Mode 7 where a "bug" in pixi-tilemap was causing the game to make hundreds of "Animation Frame Fired" calls within several millisecond periods (you can read more about this issue over on
this thread
).
EDIT
Regarding the crashing issue, it seems to be happening simply with "just" this plugin on its own (I even went so far to disable the Community_Basic plugin as a test). Any map that's close to or over 250x250 will "instantly" crash the game outright.
I will have to go back to using 2.10 until these issues are resolved.

I've just ran in to a major issue with V4 that prior versions did not seem to have.
At first I thought it was possibly just another plugin causing compatibility issues but upon testing it in a fresh project on its own, the issue was still very much prevalent.

I then made a 100x100 test map with around the same number of Region 19 autotiles and while the performance did slightly improved (averaging around 5-10FPS and using around 1.5 gigs of RAM) it was still no where within an acceptable margin of playability.
To further test that something is wrong with V4, I used the backups of V3 and V3.03 I still have to do comparisons. On the same 256x256 test map, the FPS remained perfectly stable (160-165FPS) when using V3 and dipped slightly with V3.03 (90-100FPS). The 100x100 test map also had no issues with performance (both averaging 160-165FPS). Please note that my monitor supports 165Hz so this is why MV can show these values when bringing up the FPS meter.
As far as I'm concerned, while V4 is causing severe performance issues that make things unplayable, I will have to go back to using v3/v3.03 until this issue is properly resolved.

Small map
= Less than 1.5 x screen size - If map size is over that limit, it will be considered large map and culling will be active
Culling
= Do not process sprites that are off-screen

There's no point to do culling in small maps since all sprites needs to be always drawn. In large maps culling is mandatory.
Problem was that map size check was done AFTER the cover tiles were drawn.

I wanted to point out that while v4.06 does fix tall player/event sprites, it does not fix the issue I've had regarding Yanfly's Grid-Free Doodad's.
Essentially, the problem is the way that Region 19 tiles are handled. If you place a doodad on or below a Region 19 tile, the doodad will "always" be snipped or covered by those tiles. The only way around this issue is to set the doodad to use Layer 10 (the "highest" possible layer to set a doodad to) but there's a problem with this.
Any doodad placed on Layer 6 or above will always be "above" the player and/or events (it technically needs to be on Layer 5 in order for the doodad to be "leveled" with the player and/or events so you can walk in front or behind it).
Even using a graphic editor and adding extra "space" below or above the sprite and aligning it on the map will not fix this issue.
